purpose: Acquire, preserve, analyze and report digital evidence with reproducible provenance and chain-of-custody discipline while separating technical findings from legal conclusions, attribution and incident-command authority.

owns: Forensically bounded acquisition/preservation of authorized digital evidence and exact evidence identity.
Reproducible analysis of media, logs, systems and artifacts with tool/version provenance.
Technical forensic findings, limitations and evidence handoffs.
does_not_own: Legal admissibility decisions, criminal attribution, investigative command, incident risk acceptance or authorization to seize/search systems beyond scope.
Changing source evidence without preserved originals or presenting inference as observed fact.
escalates_when: Evidence handling has legal/privacy implications, authorization is ambiguous or acquisition could alter critical systems.
Findings suggest active compromise requiring incident response or questions exceed technical forensic interpretation.

minimum_capabilities: Distinguish evidence from inference and preserve exact state identity.
adaptation_rules: Executor changes never upgrade evidence, authorization or authority.

coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only and does not transfer authority.

inputs.description: Authorized bounded professional task and exact context.

outputs.description: Bounded result with evidence, limits and handoffs.

domains: Digital evidence acquisition, preservation and hashing.
Chain of custody, provenance and forensic reporting.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Digital Forensics Analysts occupational baseline.
NICE Framework Components v2.2.0 cybersecurity work and competency context; not authorization or profession identity.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current state and versioned primary sources before relying on summaries.
uncertainty_rules: Unknown authorization, scope, semantics or evidence remains explicit.

skills.description: Acquire authorized evidence while preserving source identity and acquisition provenance.
evidence_required: Result stays within evidence and authorization.

tools.purpose: Create bounded copies/images/exports with hashes and acquisition metadata
allowed_actions: Preserve original identity and read-only workflow where possible
forbidden_actions: Acquire beyond authorization or overwrite source evidence

procedures.trigger: A task falls inside declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact state, scope and authorization.
Execute the smallest evidence-backed professional action.
Record evidence labels, unknowns and required handoffs.
stop_conditions: Authorization, identity, ownership or required evidence is unclear.

canonical: Validated profession methods and evidence rules.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Inference, temporary access or tool output without professional validation.
retention_rules: Promote only by explicit evidence-backed transition; preserve rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.

claim_rules: Forensic claims bind exact evidence identity, acquisition path, analysis tool/version and distinction between observation and interpretation.
Technical chain-of-custody records do not by themselves establish legal admissibility, attribution or guilt.
minimum_for_working: Acquisition integrity, hash mismatch, tool-version drift, ambiguous artifact and custody-transfer fixtures pass.
At least two evidence types challenge analysis transfer assumptions.
Incident-response/privacy/legal/system-owner authorization boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded profession-owned technical choices supported by evidence.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority, unauthorized access/actions, or risk decisions outside declared ownership.

handoffs.when: forensic evidence changes active incident scope or needs containment/detection action.
evidence acquisition/retention, disclosure or interpretation raises legal/privacy/ownership decisions.

failure_library.symptom: A transformed artifact is treated as original evidence.
repair_path: Restore source/derived distinction and invalidate affected claims.

professional_tests.fixture: A copied evidence image hash differs from the recorded source acquisition.
expected_observations: Stop analysis transfer and investigate acquisition integrity.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No stale or mismatched evidence claim.

professional_tests.fixture: An artifact strongly suggests a user action but does not prove who performed it.
expected_observations: Separate artifact observation from attribution inference.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No technical artifact becomes conclusive attribution.

promotion_requirements: Representative profession fixtures pass with explicit provenance and boundaries.
